Marissa —

Quick tech notes to include in the README and the KMS diagram:
- Our production serving runtime uses a split key model. Customer data is encrypted at rest with a customer-derived DEK (data encryption key) encrypted by a service KEK (key-encryption key). The KEK is managed in our KMS provider; only two internal service accounts (deployed in dedicated pods) have the ability to unwrap DEKs at runtime.
- Partners that have plaintext access: one audit/log aggregator (LogFlow Inc, listed in the CSV), and our optional analytics partner (Anomalyze) for customers who opt-in to aggregated telemetry. Both are marked with justification and retention windows in the CSV.
- Ephemeral keys: we support ephemeral session keys for burst inference workloads via our tokenized key broker — no external subprocessor holds those ephemeral keys long-term.

I've redacted internal contact emails in the CSV and added a column 'plaintext_access' (true/false) with short notes. Laura — I flagged two entries where retention windows were missing; can you fill those? Monica — I added CAIQ pointers in a draft README (see attached to me).

Karthik
Senior Reliability Engineer, Serving Runtime
